# Incident Report — MTA 2024-07-30 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.16.1.66** | Dominant internal talker in `conv,ip`; source of all NBNS/Kerberos identity traffic |
| MAC | **00:1e:64:ec:f3:08** | `eth.src` on all frames sourced from 172.16.1.66; confirmed via ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==172.16.1.66`) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-SKBR25F** | NBNS name registration `DESKTOP-SKBR25F<00>`/`<20>` from 172.16.1.66; also DNS self-registration queries `DESKTOP-SKBR25F.wiresharkworkshop.online` |
| Logged-in user | **ccollier** | Kerberos `CNameString` on TGS/AS requests from 172.16.1.66 (`ccollier`, `DESKTOP-SKBR25F$`); independently confirmed inside the malware's own C2 beacon field (see below) |

Domain: `wiresharkworkshop.online`, DC observed at 172.16.1.4 (`WIRESHARK-WS-DC`, MAC `5c:f9:dd:8c:97:35`).

## Malware Family: STRRAT

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** TCP stream 83 (172.16.1.66:49754 ↔ 141.98.10.79:12132) contains a repeating cleartext beacon that literally names the malware:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<base64>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

Field breakdown (STRRAT's known plaintext ping format): command literal `ping`, malware name `STRRAT`, victim/bot ID `1BE8292C`, hostname, username, OS, architecture, installed AV (Windows Defender), base64-encoded active window title (decodes to `Program Manager`), malware build version `1.6`, geolocated country, VM-detection flag (`Not Installed`), and process uptime counter, which increments every ~5 seconds for the full 508-second life of the stream. This exact pipe-delimited, self-labeled protocol is the documented C2 wire format of the STRRAT Java-based RAT — no signature database lookup needed, the sample identifies itself. No TLS handshake is present on this connection (raw TCP on a non-standard high port), and `141.98.10.79` was never resolved via DNS anywhere in the capture, meaning the C2 address is hardcoded in the sample — consistent with known STRRAT builds.

## Incident Timeline (relative to capture start)

| t (s) | Event |
|---|---|
| 63.97 | DNS queries for `github.com` and `repo1.maven.org` (near-simultaneous) |
| 64.77–70.63 | TLS session to 185.199.110.133, SNI `objects.githubusercontent.com` — 828 KB pulled in 6.0 s |
| 64.83 | DNS query `objects.githubusercontent.com` |
| 68.01–73.85 | TLS session to 199.232.196.209, SNI `repo1.maven.org` — **8.87 MB pulled in 5.8 s** (largest transfer in the capture) |
| 76.99 | First SYN, 172.16.1.66 → 141.98.10.79:12132 (STRRAT C2 established) |
| 77.87 | HTTP GET `ip-api.com/json/` — victim geolocation lookup (result feeds the `US:United States` field seen in the beacon seconds later) |
| 76.99 → 585.6 (end of capture) | Continuous STRRAT ping beacon every 5 seconds, ~508 s total |

The GitHub/GitHub-raw and Maven Central downloads immediately precede process execution, geolocation, and C2 beacon start with only a few seconds' gap — consistent with a staged download-and-run delivery chain (STRRAT is Java-based and commonly ships with a bundled JRE fetched at install time). This is noted as the probable delivery mechanism, not confirmed: all three sessions are TLS-encrypted, so the exact file(s) transferred, their names, and hashes are **not recoverable from this capture**.

## Indicators of Compromise

```json
{
  "victim": {
    "ip": "172.16.1.66",
    "mac": "00:1e:64:ec:f3:08",
    "hostname": "DESKTOP-SKBR25F",
    "user": "ccollier"
  },
  "malware_family": "STRRAT",
  "attribution_confidence": "signature-confirmed",
  "iocs": [
    {
      "type": "c2_endpoint",
      "value": "141.98.10.79:12132",
      "evidence": "tcp.stream==83, 172.16.1.66:49754<->141.98.10.79:12132, no TLS handshake, cleartext repeating beacon 'ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|...' every 5s for 508s; destination never resolved via DNS in the capture (hardcoded C2 IP)"
    }
  ],
  "benign_context": [
    "github.com (140.82.113.3) and objects.githubusercontent.com (185.199.110.133) - HTTPS/TLS, standard GitHub infrastructure; 828 KB transfer at t=64.8s temporally precedes infection but content unreadable (TLS)",
    "repo1.maven.org (199.232.196.209) - HTTPS/TLS, Maven Central; 8.87 MB transfer at t=68.0s temporally precedes infection but content unreadable (TLS)",
    "ip-api.com (208.95.112.1) - plaintext HTTP GET /json/, IP geolocation lookup; commonly abused by malware for victim fingerprinting but is itself a legitimate public service",
    "javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com, login.microsoftonline.com, *.msn.com, *.office.com, *.bing.com, client.wns.windows.com, and other Microsoft/Windows telemetry and update domains - standard Windows 11 / Office background traffic, unrelated to the intrusion",
    "www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt - standard Windows NCSI connectivity check"
  ],
  "incident_summary": "Windows 11 workstation DESKTOP-SKBR25F, logged in as user ccollier, was infected with the STRRAT Java-based RAT. Shortly after TLS sessions to GitHub-raw content (objects.githubusercontent.com) and Maven Central (repo1.maven.org) that likely staged the payload/runtime, the host queried ip-api.com for geolocation and then began a persistent cleartext C2 beacon to 141.98.10.79:12132 that self-identified as STRRAT and ran for the remainder of the capture."
}
```

**Caveat:** no file names or SHA256 hashes could be grounded in this evidence — the candidate delivery sessions (GitHub, Maven Central) are TLS-encrypted with no exported plaintext objects, and no `--export-objects` artifact or IDS/Suricata alert log was provided alongside the PCAP to corroborate the delivery stage. Only the C2 channel itself is directly observable in cleartext.
